Subject: Re: Intro & discovery — DataPulse realtime summarization use case

Thanks for the demo today — good to meet the team. A few notes from our side and requests as we think about pilot qualification:

- Workload: short-form summarization of user-uploaded meeting notes (avg input 800 tokens, output 80-150 tokens).
- Latency target: p95 <= 450ms for single-request interactive flows; bulk ingestion can be relaxed.
- Throughput: expected steady-state ~120 requests/min across peak shards.
- Data controls: must remain within VPC/private deployment (we can discuss Private later).

Can you share the recommended model slate for this workload, Redwood-verified TPS & latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for the models you suggested, and any prompt sets you recommend for guardrails? Also please include any test harness / perf traces for the benchmarks you ran so we can validate against our internal replay.

Attaching our sample payloads and the short product brief. Happy to sync next week for a pilot kickoff planning session.

—Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Integrations, DataPulse
alex@datapulse.ai

Subject: Fitplay follow-through: model slate, perf prooflinks & pilot kickoff

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the payloads. Recap + next steps below from our post-call alignment.

Summary of recommended slate (based on your 800-token inputs and ~150-token outputs):
- rw-falcon-lite-3b (float16) — best cost/latency balance for interactive p95 under 300–400ms in hosted mode; good first pass for quality.
- rw-3b-quant (8-bit) — lower unit cost with modest quality delta; expect ~1.6–2x TPS improvement on the same GPU profile.
- rw-13b (float16, autoscale) — target for highest quality and fewer hallucinations; anticipate higher latency/cost but stronger end-user accuracy for critical flows.

Redwood-verified performance profiles (regional/us-west2) — quick numbers from our internal bench (your sample distribution):
- rw-falcon-lite-3b: p50 75ms, p95 280ms, p99 420ms; sustained TPS ~180 (single pool, 8xA10G).
- rw-3b-quant: p50 65ms, p95 240ms, p99 380ms; sustained TPS ~320 (quant path, same pool).
- rw-13b: p50 210ms, p95 560ms, p99 920ms; sustained TPS ~60 (autoscale enabled).

Links & artifacts (attachments + links):
- Redwood eval pack (attached): redwood-eval-pack.zip — contains perf traces, prompt sets, and replay harness tailored to short summarization.
- Prompt set v1 (attached): datapulse-prompt-set-v1.jsonl — guardrails, few-shot templates, and quality checks.
- Perf summary (attached): perf-summary-datapulse.pdf — snapshot of the runs above, raw traces, and kernel selection notes.
- Verified model pages: https://app.redwood.ai/models/verified/perf?model=rw-3b-quant&region=us-west2 (example).
- Drive folder with raw traces: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/sales/DP/eval-pack-20260918

Quality/regression notes and guardrails:
- Regression risk: quantized variants (rw-3b-quant) show occasional brevity in multi-turn clarifying queries — include regression tests that assert key instruction preservation and entailment checks.
- Prompt hardening: include explicit system-level constraints in the prompt set that enforce output length, disallow invented facts, and add an allowlist for acceptable entity formatting.
- Monitoring: we recommend setting up Redwood Optimize quality monitors tied to your prompt set (we can pre-configure). Set alerts on ROUGE/precision drop > 6% vs baseline.

Requested next steps (proposed timeline):
1) We’ll upload the tailored eval pack (attached) into your Drive and run the replay harness against your sample payloads — action: Stephanie/Ben by EOD 9/19.
2) Joint pilot kickoff to align SLOs and pilot success criteria — propose 9/22 or 9/23 (30–45m).
3) If pilot fits, scope Dedicated or Private deployment (procurement required) — Naomi to own procurement pathing.

Technical notes: Ben added a few infra recommendations below on batching and KV cache settings.

Attachments: redwood-eval-pack.zip, datapulse-prompt-set-v1.jsonl, perf-summary-datapulse.pdf

Let me know if you want the perf runs repeated on a different instance type — we can reproduce on T4/A10G/A100 profiles.

—Stephanie Nguyen

Looping in a couple of infra specifics that matter for the throughput/latency numbers above:

- Batch sizing: for rw-3b-quant we used a dynamic batching window tuned to 15–25ms with a max batch size of 32 for your payload distribution; that is how we hit ~320 TPS. If you prioritize lower p95, we can reduce the window but TPS drops.
- KV cache: enable per-user KV caching for multi-turn clarifications — reduces repeated prefix work and improves p50 by 12–18% in our tests.
- Autoscaling policy for rw-13b: set a conservative scale-up threshold at 65% GPU util to avoid p99 spikes; add a burst capacity pool for peak ingestion windows.
- Quantization caveat: 8-bit paths require tuned dequant kernels; expect small quality differences on entity formatting. We included a regression checklist in the eval pack under /regression_checks.md.

I can spin a reproducible bench on the exact instance type you want; tell me which GPU family (A10G preferred for cost/latency balance) and I’ll attach a concise run summary to the Drive folder.

—Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
